summary: SpaceX launched its Starship vehicle into orbit for the first time during a test flight, though the mission ended early. In civil spaceflight, NASA and Boeing updated development plans for the Commercial Crew Program, targeting an uncrewed Starliner flight no earlier than December with a follow-up crewed mission planned for 2028. The timeline updates come as NASA faces a reported funding cut of over 50 percent to its fiscal year 2025 planetary research and analysis budget, even as international diplomatic participation grew with the Artemis Accords surpassing 75 signatories. On the scientific front, researchers discovered a lunar "magnetic fossil" in China's Chang'e-6 returned samples, astronomers identified a radio galaxy displaying evidence of four distinct jet outbursts, and distant hydrogen emissions provided a new approach to investigating dark energy. In defense developments, the U.S. Space Force expressed interest in leveraging commercial antennas for satellite control, while U.S. and UK forces jointly tested SM-6 missiles on a target frigate during a sinking exercise, amid warnings from Air Force and industry officials that a continuing resolution could delay Collaborative Combat Aircraft production. In commercial sector news, Meridian Space spun out from SpinLaunch, and NASA completed testing on a dual-mode propulsion CubeSat ahead of its launch. Looking ahead, observers should watch for the upcoming launch of Star Catcher’s orbital power-beaming demonstration.
